business_scope.primary_industry_name: Zinc Alloy Die-Casting and Tampo Printing of 1:18 Scale Car Replicas

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system with significant Common Law influence in corporate, commercial, banking, and maritime practice; Hague Apostille Convention member since 1992; United States Dollar as legal tender)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations) as amended by Law 366 of 31 January 2023; Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework) as amended by Law 70 of 2019 and Law 102 of 2020; Executive Decree 202 of 2015 (Consolidated AML/CFT Regulation) and its implementing resolutions; Law 254 of 27 August 2020 (creation of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros and mandatory ultimate beneficial owner declarations filed with the Registro Público; 10% direct or indirect ownership threshold for capital-holding persons, with the FATF 25% floor applied for low-risk entity classification); Law 52 of 27 October 2016 (tax transparency and automatic exchange of information).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, council members, protector, and authorized signatories against: (i) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists; (ii) United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) HMT UK Sanctions List; (v) Panama's national PEP and designated-persons list administered by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); and (vi) GAFILAT public statements on high-risk jurisdictions. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEP status, nationality or residence in a FATF high-risk jurisdiction, or any inconsistency in source-of-funds documentation. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years as required by Law 23 of 2015 and Executive Decree 202 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Online Name Reservation Module (www.registro-publico.gob.pa), also accessible through the Panamá Digital e-government gateway
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in Spanish or in any language using Latin script; the Public Registry applies phonetic and visual similarity tests against existing corporations, foundations, and registered trade names; the name must incorporate the statutory identifier 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or its accepted equivalent; non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into official Panamanian Spanish orthography.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: CÁMARA DE COMERCIO / CHAMBER OF COMMERCE
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection the applicant receives an electronic notice with a discrepancy code. The applicant may file a reconsideration request (reclamo) with the Dirección de Servicios en Línea within five (5) business days, attaching a comparative name-search report and up to two alternative name proposals. If the reconsideration is refused, a formal administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) may be submitted to the Director General del Registro Público within ten (10) business days. Final judicial review is available through the contentious-administrative chamber (Sala Tercera) of the Corte Suprema de Justicia. A rejected name may be re-filed only with documented written consent from the earlier registrant or with a materially distinctive added element.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A private interest foundation must maintain a registered office in Panama at the physical address of its licensed resident agent under Law 25 of 1995 as amended by Law 366 of 2023. A purely virtual or co-working mailbox is not acceptable for the statutory seat; however, a digital-only operational correspondence address is permissible for royalty, licensing, and low-risk commercial activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 10–15% probability over a five-year lifecycle) for an asset-holding, non-operating PIF with no real estate, no local employees, and no physical inventory. Probability rises to approximately 35–40% if the PIF later registers with the Dirección General de Ingresos for local taxable activities or holds Panamanian real estate; for the die-cast scale-model licensing scope, physical presence is satisfied by the resident agent's office and no unannounced factory-equivalent inspection is expected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended; principal formation, endowment, Foundation Council and registry provisions (Articles 1–7, 13–19, 25–31)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Dirección de Personas Jurídicas – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado / Private Interest Foundation Formation Deed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Initial endowment must be at least US$10,000 or equivalent in assets; the Founder must declare the endowment in the Foundation Charter, and the Foundation Council must enter it in the asset ledger. No escrow or government custody account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED THAT the Foundation Charter submitted by the Founder is unanimously approved and adopted; the initial endowment of US$10,000, declared in the Charter, is accepted and credited to the Foundation's asset ledger; the registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], City of Panama, and [LAW FIRM] is appointed as Resident Agent; [NAME] is appointed President and [NAME] Secretary of the Foundation Council, with authority to open banking accounts, execute facility leases, and instruct the Resident Agent to complete all Public Registry filings; and the President or Secretary is authorized individually to sign regulatory filings and to procure all operational licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the First Judicial Circuit of Panama (competent Panamanian Notary Public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Foundation Charter must be drafted in Spanish and presented before a Panamanian notary. The Founder and the Resident Agent must execute the deed before the notary, who will authenticate the signatures and the endowment declaration. After incorporation in the notarial protocol, request a testimonio of the deed for Public Registry filing.
required_dossiers: Passport or official ID of each Founder
Foundation Charter in Spanish
Signed Resident Agent acceptance
Declaration of initial endowment assets valued at minimum US$10,000
Notarized Power of Attorney if Founder appears by representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial review identifies a missing or conflicting provision, prepare a correction addendum or new deed before signature; if a power of attorney is used, it must be apostilled or legalized by the Panamanian consulate before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección de Personas Jurídicas, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the testimonio and required form to the Public Registry's Foundation Section. Pay the official registry fee, obtain the filing receipt, and wait for issuance of the Private Interest Foundation Registration Certificate. The Resident Agent follows the case status online and collects the stamped certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Deed
Testimonio (certified notarial copy) for Public Registry
Foundation registration form signed by the Resident Agent
Registry fee payment receipt
Identity document of the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry issues a 'razón de impedimento', correct the identified defect and resubmit within ten business days; if the issue concerns the name or registered office, file a modification and pay the additional registry fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance – online via Panamatramites.gob.pa / SICOR portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) of the Foundation. Select the economic activity code for manufacturing of collectible die-cast model vehicles (ISIC 3240/NAICS 339930). Obtain the taxpayer certificate and retain evidence of territorial-source income segregation for the foundation's eventual Panamanian-source tax obligations.
required_dossiers: Private Interest Foundation Registration Certificate
Certified copy of the Foundation Charter
RUC application form completed by the Resident Agent
Passport or ID of each Foundation Council member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI queries the activity code or the foundation's non-commercial purpose, submit a written explanation with the Charter and a description of the die-casting activity; DGI will update the RUC without penalty if the correction is made before the first tax filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and Business Patent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas Municipales (Municipal Revenue Directorate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación for the die-casting and tampo-printing facility. Calculate the municipal business patent fee based on the estimated annual gross revenue or fiscal capital, pay the applicable amount, and obtain the municipal operating permit before machinery installation or production.
required_dossiers: DGI RUC certificate
Private Interest Foundation Registration Certificate
Lease agreement or ownership certificate for the industrial facility
Plans and written description of die-casting and tampo-printing operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality challenges the declared estimated revenue, file an administrative reconsideration with the Municipal Revenue Directorate, attaching a certified asset schedule and sworn production estimates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industria; Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the environmental impact classification questionnaire and obtain the relevant Environmental Impact Assessment resolution. Where required, register the industrial establishment with MICI; secure approval before importing or installing die-casting furnaces, dust collectors and VOC control equipment.
required_dossiers: Municipal Aviso de Operación
Environmental impact classification form
Process flow description for zinc alloy die-casting and tampo printing
Waste and solvent management plan
Technical drawings of the ventilation and wastewater pretreatment systems
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MiAMBIENTE reclassifies the project or issues a request for supplementary information, instruct a licensed environmental consultant to complete the required EIA study and submit the additional analyses within 30 business days; MICI authorization remains conditional until the environmental resolution is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety and Occupational Health Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) – Dirección de Salud y Seguridad Ocupacional
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange the fire-safety inspection and obtain the annual fire certificate for the facility. Register the foundation as employer with the CSS if workers are hired, and complete the workplace health-and-safety inspection covering noise, ventilation, personal protective equipment, emergency exits and die-casting machinery guarding.
required_dossiers: Building occupancy or structural certificate
Fire alarm, extinguisher and emergency exit installation plans
Health and safety manual
Die-casting machine risk assessments
CSS employer registration form and employee roster
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any fire or structural deficiencies noted in the inspection report and request a re-inspection within 10 business days; if MITRADEL identifies airborne metal or solvent exposure, install engineering controls and submit a compliance report before resuming production.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industria, in coordination with Municipalidad de Panamá
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Industrial / Municipal Industrial Operating License; no separate sectoral concession is required for ISIC 3240

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección Nacional de Normativa e Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II (Moderate Impact) – Environmental Impact Registration or Preliminary Environmental Impact Study, depending on installed die-casting capacity; a full EIA report is required if annual metal throughput exceeds 200 metric tons.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater must meet the applicable MiAMBIENTE and municipal sewage standards: pH 6.0–9.0, total suspended solids ≤ 350 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand ≤ 1,000 mg/L, zinc ≤ 5 mg/L, lead ≤ 0.5 mg/L, copper ≤ 1.0 mg/L, and no free cyanide. VOC emissions from die-casting and tampo printing must be captured by mechanical ventilation and comply with the approved MiAMBIENTE emissions register; spent die-casting oil, inks, solvents and dust must be manifested and disposed of by an authorized hazardous waste handler, with disposal records retained for at least five years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá covering die-casting furnaces, LPG storage, electrical installations and fire egress; structural load approval for the industrial floor and any mezzanine from the Municipal Buildings Directorate; and workplace clearance from MITRADEL under Panama's occupational health and safety legislation, including noise control, air contaminant exposure, personal protective equipment and emergency response; CSS employer registration is also required for work-injury coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; official electronic portal: 'Sede Electrónica DGI' (e-Tax) and the DGI Facturación Electrónica platform at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa/; customs counterpart for export control: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (i) Execute the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) charter before a Panamanian notary and record it in the Registro Público under Law 25 of 12 June 1995; (ii) appoint a licensed resident agent in Panama and maintain a registered office; (iii) apply through the DGI Sede Electrónica for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), the statutory TIN and VAT-equivalent ID, submitting the foundation certificate, registered charter, resident agent appointment, and registered-office proof; (iv) simultaneously register the PIF as an ITBMS taxpayer in the general regime (or the simplified regime if eligible) and enrol in the mandatory electronic invoicing system; (v) open a Panamanian bank account and associate it with the RUC to receive export proceeds through SWIFT wire or PayPal remittances.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — A PIF is a separate legal person subject to entity-level taxation (not a pass-through), and Panama applies a territorial income tax model under the Código Tributario: only Panama-source income is taxable. Export income from the sale of die-cast scale automotive models (ISIC 3240) delivered to foreign buyers is generally excluded from Panamanian-source ISR; the foundation's assets held for private-interest purposes are likewise outside the ISR net unless commercial activity is carried on in Panama.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or entity-classification election exists under Panamanian law; the PIF cannot elect pass-through treatment and has no hybrid-election mechanism. Available statutory elections within the target facts: (a) election to apply the Régimen Simplificado de ITBMS for small taxpayers whose annual taxable turnover does not exceed approximately B/. 60,000, and (b) election to treat qualifying exports as zero-rated ITBMS supplies. Panama has adopted OECD hybrid-mismatch reporting and, if a mismatched tax outcome arises from another jurisdiction disregarding the PIF, DGI will neutralise it domestically by denying the deduced benefit.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's value-added tax on movable goods and services)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general-regime exemption threshold: any person engaged in taxable industrial or commercial activity in Panama, including a PIF conducting die-casting and tampo printing, must register for ITBMS before issuing its first invoice regardless of volume. A simplified fixed-contribution regime (Régimen Simplificado) is available only to micro and small enterprises with annual gross sales at or below approximately B/. 60,000; the target manufacturing operation exceeding that volume must register in the general regime and file monthly ITBMS returns.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing ('Factura Electrónica'). All general-regime taxpayers must issue e-invoices through DGI-authorised technological service providers; each invoice is transmitted to the DGI platform in near real time and receives a unique Código Único de Facturación (CUF). There is no physical fiscal stamp; fiscal clearance is digital. For exports, the e-invoice must carry the zero-rated export indicator and must be linked to the corresponding customs e-DUA. Failure to comply disentitles the taxpayer to ITBMS input credits and to zero-rating claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods — including zinc alloy die-cast 1:18 scale car replicas — are zero-rated under ITBMS when the goods are definitively removed from Panamanian territory and sold to a non-resident buyer. Eligibility requires: (i) a customs export declaration electronically filed with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA); (ii) physical departure of the goods from Panama within the declared period; (iii) commercial transport documents evidencing the foreign destination; (iv) payment received in convertible currency through the Panamanian banking system, including SWIFT wire or PayPal credits deposited into the PIF's Panamanian bank account; and (v) retention of the inward-remittance certificate. Export services directly related to the exported goods are also zero-rated. Input ITBMS attributable to zero-rated export sales is creditable and refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Documento Único de Aduanas, e-DUA) validated and exit-certified by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (Conocimiento de Embarque) identifying the foreign consignee and the port of discharge outside Panama
Electronic invoice (Factura Electrónica) containing the CUF, the zero-rated export indicator, and the 0% ITBMS line
Inward remittance certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) issued by a Panamanian bank confirming collection of proceeds via SWIFT wire or PayPal credit
Foreign sales contract or purchase order, packing list, and transport insurance documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI and ANA jointly audit zero-rated export transactions on both documentary and physical verification bases; fictitious exports, inflated declared values, misdeclared destinations, or non-repatriation of proceeds are treated as fiscal fraud. Consequences under the Código Tributario, as amended by Law 76 of 2019, include reassessment and restitution of the avoided 7% ITBMS, default interest and regulatory surcharges, and substantial fines, which in aggravated cases may reach up to 100% of the omitted tax. Wilful fraudulent export claims constitute criminal tax evasion and may result in imprisonment. DGI may additionally cancel the taxpayer's e-invoicing authorisation, block refunds of input ITBMS credits, and apply extended limitation periods where export documentation is falsified.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank exists in Panama; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the banking and financial regulator, and the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) oversees fiscal and financial policy. The U.S. dollar is legal tender and the national currency, so foreign exchange administration functions are effectively replaced by a dollarized monetary system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized economy with unrestricted convertibility. No separate legal tender exists, and the U.S. dollar circulates freely. Both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible without foreign exchange approval. Profit remittances, dividends, interest, and royalties are freely transferable abroad through the banking system with no quantitative limits, withholding only applying under domestic tax law for Panama-source income. No restrictions on the repatriation of capital or dividends for non-resident equity holders in a Private Interest Foundation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no export proceeds surrender requirement and does not mandate conversion of export receipts into any domestic currency because the U.S. dollar is the legal tender. Foreign currency earned from exports may be retained in any bank account, locally or abroad, and used freely for trade or other payments without any statutory timeline or compulsory conversion ratio.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC International Bank Inc. – Panamanian Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low to Medium. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are not automatically recognized as licensed banks or regulated payment service providers under Panamanian law. They may offer ancillary cross-border payment facilitation only through a local licensed bank or through a Panama-registered non-bank financial intermediary. Direct operation without a physical Panamanian agent or a licensed local partner is legally constrained. The SBP does not issue a pure 'EMI license' equivalent to the EU framework, and any payment intermediation into Panama's banking system requires compliance with the SBP's criminal, anti-money laundering, and consumer protection circulars.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively required. Directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners must personally appear before a Panamanian notary and the bank's compliance officer or a designated correspondent agent to execute account opening documents and undergo a face-to-face interview. Remote opening is generally not permitted for non-resident clients; however, some banks may allow a notarized power of attorney granted to a local attorney-in-fact or a Panamanian legal representative, subject to stricter enhanced due diligence and additional background verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner opacity under Panama's 2015 Beneficial Ownership Law
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SBP-compliant registry filing certificate, notarized foundation charter and bylaws, list of foundation council members and protectors, sworn declaration of beneficial ownership, and certified copies of passports for all ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to demonstrate source of funds and source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully audited financial statements or management accounts, bank reference letters from existing lenders, tax returns in the entity's country of residence, and documented proof of the origin of the initial capital injection from die-casting and scale-model manufacturing activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to high-risk counterparties or tax-haven jurisdictions identified by the bank's AML policy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial contracts with customers and suppliers, proforma invoices and shipping documents, bills of lading, certificates of origin, and third-party sanctions and adverse-media screening reports demonstrating no links to prohibited jurisdictions or politically exposed persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person status of any director, beneficiary, or trusted advisor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Net-worth statement, source-of-wealth questionnaire, independent wealth manager or legal counsel attestation, and a commitment letter to submit to enhanced ongoing monitoring and beneficial ownership disclosures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers to the foundation's USD-denominated operational bank account in Panama. No exchange control approval or import license is required. Beneficiary bank details, foundation legal name, and the registration number from the Registro Público de Panamá must be included to satisfy the receiving bank's compliance. The intended purpose should be clearly stated as 'equity contribution to foundation' or 'operating capital injection', and supporting board resolutions must be retained for AML verification. Correspondent banks in the U.S. may request the originator's full legal name, address, and purpose code; all incoming funds are credited in U.S. dollars with no conversion requirement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for manufacturing inputs and finished die-cast collectibles are made primarily by SWIFT MT103 for direct wire payments, with MT202 for interbank transfers when intermediary institutions are involved. For medium and large transactions involving international suppliers, commercial letters of credit (L/C) opened by the Panamanian bank with SWIFT MT700/MT707 messages are used as the principal clearing rail. Documentary collections (CAD or D/P) via SWIFT MT400 may also be used. All disbursements must reference the commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading to support the underlying trade. Since Panama is dollar-based, no foreign exchange conversion occurs for invoicing in USD; non-USD trade settlements are executed through bank-provided FX contracts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards against the U.S. dollar (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/CNY) for non-USD trade payables and receivables
Cross-currency swaps between USD and major trading currencies to manage longer-term cash flow positions
FX options purchased from licensed Panamanian banks for hedging currency exposure on non-USD sourcing or distribution contracts

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be permitted only where the counterparty is an international bank with a registered Panama branch or a licensed offshore bank operating under the SBP, but their use is secondary as the local currency is the USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a reinstatement penalty of USD 300 plus applicable surcharges and interest; failure to pay for two consecutive fiscal years exposes the foundation to administrative strike-off and loss of legal capacity to operate or transfer assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial-Owner Declaration ('Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final')
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Official Registry Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filable each year between 1 January and 31 March for the preceding calendar year; newly incorporated foundations file within 60 days of registry inscription.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Law 254 of 2021, penalties range from USD 1,000 up to USD 100,000; continuous non-compliance may result in suspension of the foundation's certified legal standing and the risk of administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (through the appointed resident agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, typically aligned with the franchise-tax payment and due by 30 June; any change of agent must be filed immediately.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lack of a registered resident agent after the statutory grace period triggers legal representation cancellation; the foundation cannot validly enter contracts, litigate, or perform banking procedures until a new agent is qualified and recorded.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (if Panamanian-sourced income arises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three months after the fiscal year-end; for most entities with calendar-year close, due 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 5% of the tax due up to USD 5,000, plus monthly interest at the statutory rate; misleading or non-filing can trigger criminal tax-fraud sanctions and a freeze on the foundation's taxpayer ID.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995 solely because of its legal form. However, an independent CPA audit is mandatory when the foundation's Panamanian-sourced gross income exceeds USD 3.0 million or total assets exceed USD 5.0 million in a fiscal year; voluntary audited statements may be required by lenders or commercial counterparties.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: A foundation engaged in commercial manufacturing must maintain accounting records in Spanish using US-dollar denomination, applying Panama's adopted version of IFRS; smaller operations may apply IFRS for SMEs ('NIIF para PYMES').

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 254 of 2021 requires the foundation and its resident agent to file an annual confirmation of the ultimate beneficial owners of each class of rights, including any changes resulting from transfers of beneficiary interests. Every transfer must be recorded in the foundation's internal registry and submitted through the resident agent within the annual filing window; failing to disclose a transfer is treated as a separate, directly punishable omission.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Founders and Beneficiaries (Registro de Fundadores y Beneficiarios)
Register of Council Members / Guardians (Registro del Consejo de Fundación)
Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro UBO)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 7,500 per annum if the statutory audit threshold is met; otherwise zero for a fully exempt foundation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial income tax system: only Panama-source income is subject to the 25% headline rate. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) conducting die-cast manufacturing in Panama is taxed at the standard rate on net manufacturing profit sourced in Panama. No statutory tax holiday applies to general die-cast manufacturing; income derived from exports remains taxable when the economic activity (production and transfer of title) takes place in Panama. Limited preferential rates are available only under specific FDI/production incentive regimes (e.g., free zone or special economic zone treatment), which are elective and subject to separate licensing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 61 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta) – Annual corporate income tax return. Filed electronically through the TUA platform of the Panamanian Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) at www.dgi.gob.pa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (calendar fiscal year ending 31 December; alternate fiscal years require DGI approval).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Form 61 annual return must be filed no later than 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end. Monthly advance income tax payments (pagos directos) must be filed by the 15th of the following month on Form 415 or through TUA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RUC (tax ID), fiscal year, registered address and economic activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF must have a local agent obtain a Panama RUC and list the local address of the registered foundation office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 – Ingresos gravables de fuente panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from manufacturing sales of scale die-cast automotive models, including all proceeds from domestic and export sales, where the production and delivery risk pass in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Panama-sourced revenue. Foreign-source income earned through a fixed place of business abroad is excluded only if no Panama operational activity is involved and is separately documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly attributable to Panamanian operations: raw materials (zinc alloy, paint, decals), payroll, factory depreciation, utilities, freight, and authorized royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All expenses must be supported by invoices and bank records. Related-party charges require transfer pricing documentation at the time of filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income after application of eligible deductions and the five-year loss carryforward limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the carryforward amount and attach a reconciliation; non-resident foundations may not use foreign-loss carryforwards against Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 25 – Impuesto sobre la Renta Liquidado
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax liability at the 25% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foundation may credit any advance payments already made via the local tax agent's TUA portal; no additional withholding is levied on the filing itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Anexo – Operaciones con Partes Relacionadas (Transfer Pricing Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all controlled transactions with related enterprises: raw-material purchases, management fees, licenses, interest, and intercompany sales of die-cast models.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when annual Panama-source gross revenue exceeds USD 1.5 million or related-party transactions exceed USD 2 million aggregate. Provide a summary of the TP method used and audited financial statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 61 triggers a fine of 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of a month, up to a maximum of 50% of the tax. Late tax payment incurs a monthly surcharge of 1% on the unpaid amount (max 30%). Failure to file electronically may attract additional procedural fines up to USD 10,000. Repeated non-compliance can lead to RUC suspension, forced assessment, and an automatic assessment penalty of 10% of the DGI's determined tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (Panama-source dividend distribution). The tax is levied on all dividends paid by a Panama-registered entity, including a PIF, from Panama-source profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's double tax treaties (e.g., with Mexico, Spain, the Netherlands, South Korea, UAE) may reduce the dividend withholding rate to between 0% and 10%, typically subject to a minimum shareholding of 10-15% and a 365-day shareholding period. Administrative protocol for relief: (i) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residency (TRC) from the recipient's home-country tax authority; (ii) present the TRC and a beneficial ownership certificate (Form DD / vendor declaration) to the Panamanian withholding agent; (iii) complete the DGI's online treaty-relief filing in TUA before or at the time of the dividend distribution; (iv) retain the documentation for at least five years. No advance ruling is required for treaty-resident portfolio shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents is subject to a statutory withholding of 5% on the gross amount, reduced under treaties to 0-5% for beneficial owners such as banks. Royalties for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment or for trademarks and know-how paid to non-residents attract a statutory withholding of 10% on the gross amount; treaty rates generally range from 5% to 10% for rights used in Panama.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File (and Master File, where applicable) is triggered where the taxpayer's aggregate related-party transactions in the fiscal year exceed B/.2,000,000 (USD 2,000,000) or where the taxpayer's gross annual Panama-source income exceeds B/.1,500,000 (USD 1,500,000). A Master File is additionally required for multinational groups with consolidated turnover of USD 50 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), introduced by Executive Decree 261 of 2018 and amended by Decree 108 of 2021, are applicable to legal entities, including PIFs, carrying on 'relevant activities' and deriving income from outside Panama. Die-cast scale-model manufacturing itself is not a statutorily listed relevant activity; however, if the foundation generates IP-holding, distribution, financing, or headquarters income, it must demonstrate (i) local management and control, (ii) adequate local employees, premises, and expenditure, and (iii) full local bookkeeping and accounting records. A PIF with physical factory operations in Panama and substantive local payroll automatically satisfies the purpose test for manufacturing and would not be treated as a purely offshore shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission or concealment of Panama-source manufacturing sales revenue from die-cast scale automotive models, or deliberate inflation of deductible costs, in Form 61 filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% of the tax evaded plus monthly interest at the rate of 1% of the amount due until payment; criminal conviction for tax fraud carries a penalty of imprisonment from 2 to 6 years, disqualification from commercial activity for up to 5 years, and a monetary fine equivalent to two to ten times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Person who signs or validates a false tax return is jointly and severally liable for all unpaid taxes, fines, and interest; in the presence of fraudulent intention, the director may face civil restitution of the tax amount, a court-ordered travel ban, and imprisonment term of up to 6 years. The corporate veil is pierced when the foundation is used as a mere instrumentality to commit fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Foundation and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the Private Interest Foundation solely as an invoicing shell for die-cast sales without any local office, employees, operational risk, or business substance in Panama, while filing no income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may disregard the foundation for tax purposes, assess unreported Panama-source income at 25%, impose fines of 5% per month up to 50% of the tax, and levy a 10% surcharge for late filing. Additionally, an unlicensed fiduciary front may be sanctioned by the Superintendency of Banks with fines between USD 10,000 and USD 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally responsible for the tax liability under the doctrine of alter ego where the foundation is undercapitalized and commingles assets; they face criminal charges for fraudulent simulation and may be subject to heritage and patrimonial attachment orders and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Arm's-Length Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and retain Local/Master File, not reporting controlled transactions, or setting non-arm's-length prices for intercompany sale of die-cast collectibles, royalty payments, or management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment to arm's-length prices; penalty of 40% on the entire adjustment; if the taxpayer fails to present documentation on time, a fixed penalty of 1% of the transaction value, capped where otherwise lawfully applicable; automatic anti-avoidance fines for structures with no commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax officers who sign the TP report and knowingly use false pricing data may be fined personally up to USD 10,000; in flagrant cases, the accountant or director may be charged with tax fraud for facilitating the mispricing, subject to imprisonment and civil damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving mobile/digital payments (PayPal) or Swift wire transfers from customers and failing to maintain basic AML/KYC records, failing to report designated transactions above USD 10,000 to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF), or using the PIF to mask the true purchaser.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama AML Law 23 of 2015, unlicensed non-financial designated businesses engaged in certain commercial activities must register with the UAF and are subject to fines up to USD 1,000,000; failure to file STRs/CTRs may result in license revocation, and the underlying funds may be subject to forfeiture in rem actions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit the PIF to be utilized for money laundering (e.g., layering payments from suspect jurisdictions) face criminal liability up to 12 years' imprisonment, civil liability for laundered value, personal peace and travel bans pending trial, and consequent disqualification as directors of any Panamanian entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distribution of profits from the foundation's Panamanian manufacturing activities to non-resident beneficiaries without deducting and paying the mandatory 10% dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The foundation remains liable for the unpaid 10% dividend tax, plus a surcharge of 20% of the unpaid amount and late-payment interest at 1% monthly; the DGI may also issue a default judgment for the grossed-up amount and suspend the RUC, preventing imports and exporting licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve a dividend distribution knowing that the 10% withholding tax has not been paid are jointly and severally liable for the tax plus surcharge; the DGI may obtain a civil judgment against them, freeze personal assets, and the directors may be criminally prosecuted if they stripped the foundation's assets to render the foundation insolvent.
